newsitem.title: VATICAN: Castro faces "Last Judgment" in Sistine Chapel.
newsitem.headline: Castro faces "Last Judgment" in Sistine Chapel.

text.p: Fidel Castro came face to face with God's mercy and wrath on Tuesday.
The veteran communist Cuban president was awe-struck when he viewed Michelangelo's "Last Judgment" fresco in the Sistine Chapel after his historic meeting with Pope John Paul.
He stood in wonder as he gazed at the 160 square metre (1,720 square feet) "Last Judgment" -- a dizzying swirl of 336 figures depicting Michelangelo's fearsome vision of humankind's final moments.
Castro, schooled by Jesuit priests as a child, got a private guided tour of one of the world's most priceless art treasures.
Looking up at the ceiling, his gaze fixed on what is perhaps the most famous scene in art history -- the arm of a bearded God reaching out to give life to Adam in the act of creation.
"Una maravilla," (a marvel) he said softly, as if to himself, in scenes recorded by a Vatican television team.
Michelangelo finished painting the Sistine frescoes in 1541, 49 years after Christopher Columbus discovered Cuba during his first voyage to the New World.
The frescoes in the chapel, where conclaves are held to elect popes, underwent a 14-year restoration project that ended in 1994 and revived their original brillance.
